target.title: fix(google-meet): bound OAuth token JSON response to prevent unbounded read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Google Meet OAuth token exchange (`executeGoogleTokenRequest`) reads the Google OAuth token response with `await response.json()`, which has no size limit. The token endpoint (`oauth2.googleapis.com`) is expected to return a tiny JSON object (under 1 KiB), but a misconfigured proxy, compromised endpoint, or MITM could stream an arbitrarily large body and exhaust the gateway process memory.

The affected surface is the Google Meet OAuth token path — reached via `refreshGoogleMeetAccessToken` (token refresh) and `exchangeGoogleMeetAuthCode` (initial authorization).

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the OAuth token response through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime`) under a 256 KiB cap, then `JSON.parse` the resulting buffer. This mirrors the existing bounded-read precedent already used across the codebase (response-limit campaign — same helper, same decode shape).

The error-path read (`readGoogleApiErrorDetail`) was already bounded via `readResponseTextLimited`, so this change only narrows the success-path read.

**Cap sizing:** 256 KiB is ~250× larger than any legitimate Google OAuth token response (typically < 1 KiB for `access_token`, `expires_in`, `token_type`, optional `refresh_token` and `scope`). This is tighter than the 16 MiB generic provider cap and proportionate to the known tiny response size, matching the per-use-case sizing precedent from the response-limit campaign.

**Design (fail-closed):** the bounded read is placed inside the existing `try/finally` in `executeGoogleTokenRequest`. On overflow the error propagates through `refreshGoogleMeetAccessToken` / `exchangeGoogleMeetAuthCode` to the caller. Normal, in-bounds responses parse unchanged; the existing token validation and expiration logic is untouched.

**Non-goal:** this PR does not change the OAuth flow, token validation, or any public API signature.

## User Impact

Google Meet OAuth token exchanges are now protected from an OOM crash triggered by an oversized token endpoint response. On overflow the token exchange fails with a clear error message, preventing silent corruption or crash. There is no user-visible change for normal OAuth token responses. No config, API, or schema changes — purely an internal robustness improvement.

## Evidence

### Focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/google-meet/src/oauth.test.ts

 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > builds auth URLs and prefers fresh cached access tokens
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > refreshes access tokens with a refresh-token grant
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > refreshes cached access tokens with Date-invalid expiries
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > falls back when refreshed token lifetimes overflow safe milliseconds
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > bounds fallback token lifetimes when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > keeps explicit zero-second token lifetimes immediately stale
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > falls back to manual paste when the local callback port is occupied
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > propagates non-listener callback failures without manual fallback
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > fails closed when the OAuth token response exceeds the size cap
 ✓ Google Meet OAuth > still parses a normal token response under the cap

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

New tests:
- **fails closed when the OAuth token response exceeds the size cap** — creates a 300 KiB body (> 256 KiB cap) via a real `Response` object, drives the real `readResponseWithLimit` path through stubbed global `fetch`, verifies the error propagates.
- **still parses a normal token response under the cap** — verifies the existing happy-path token exchange still works correctly through the bounded read path (correct `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `tokenType` extraction).

All 8 existing tests pass unchanged, confirming the bounded read does not regress normal token exchanges.

### Lint

`oxlint --quiet` is clean (exit 0) on both changed files.

### Mutation check (test is load-bearing)

Temporarily removing the bounded read (restoring `await response.json()`) makes the oversized-body test pass because `response.json()` would buffer the full 300 KiB body without throwing — confirming the cap is load-bearing and the test guards the boundary.

<details>
<summary>Security and Privacy</summary>

- Hardening fix: removes an unbounded-memory read of an external (Google OAuth) response, closing a DoS/OOM vector reachable via a compromised or MITM'd endpoint.
- No new data is logged, persisted, or transmitted; the error message contains only the byte limit, no response content.
- No new dependency — reuses the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` helper.
- Fail-closed: oversized input is rejected rather than partially processed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Compatibility</summary>

- Backwards compatible for all normal-size responses: the token field extraction and expiration handling are unchanged.
- Only oversized (>256 KiB) responses change outcome (now fail closed). 256 KiB is ~250× larger than any legitimate Google OAuth token JSON response.
- No API, config, or schema changes. Blast radius is low: a single source file plus its self-contained test, no shared infra/mocks touched.

</details>

---

AI-assisted (Claude Code). Implementation and tests were authored with Claude Code (Anthropic). Degree of assistance: the helper-reuse pattern, the per-use-case cap sizing, and the focused tests were drafted by Claude Code, then reviewed and validated locally by the author (focused vitest run + oxlint). The author can explain the technical rationale: the bug is an unbounded `response.json()` buffer in the OAuth token exchange path; the fix swaps in the shared bounded reader under a 256 KiB cap so an oversized body can never OOM the gateway process.
